comment: XR RELEASE MANIFEST — the single source of truth for release identity and every public claim. Constitution Article XXII.1 ('One release manifest stamps version across version.ts, package.json, README, installers, website ... CI fails on drift') and Article XIX.1 ('no public claim without an evidence link'). Edit THIS file, then run `bun run release:stamp`. Never hand-edit a stamped surface. NOTE (2026-08-13): 1.0.0 is a DELIBERATE semver rebaseline of 7.1.0 (Truth) — the same codebase, re-identified as the first stable line. Historical 7.x artifacts remain under docs/ as frozen records. INDEPENDENT VERSION LINES (deliberate, not drift): mobile/package.json (PWA line, e.g. 28.x) and cloud/package.json (control-plane line, e.g. 1.0.x) version independently of the product line and are NOT stamped targets; website/src/lib/site.ts is the stamped console surface.

identity.name: @rrrtx/xr
identity.description: XR — a local-first, provider-neutral AI agent runtime. BYOK, spend-capped, tamper-evident audit, plugin/MCP extensibility.
identity.author: Muhammad Ahmad (@ahmadrrrtx)

channels.comment: Public release channels (launch-audit XR-LAUNCH-001/002; owner decisions D1 + D6, 2026-10-22). identity.version is the in-development line on main; publicVersion is what EVERY public install path serves today. The bootstrap installers are stamped from publicVersion (bun run release:stamp), and `bun run channel:live` asserts each claimed channel serves exactly publicVersion with bytes matching that release's signed SHA256SUMS. Promote publicVersion only after the new release's live channel check passes (docs/release/CHANNELS.md#public-version). withdrawnTags exist in git but were never published: their GitHub releases must be marked pre-release and npm must never carry them (scripts/tag-npm-invariant.ts).

withdrawnTags.reason: Release run 38663173550 failed at its gates job (Identity + claim + channel gates, exit 2), so no CLI binaries, SHA256SUMS, npm tarball, Docker image or channel manifests were produced. The GitHub release only carries 5 unsigned desktop bundles attached by desktop-app.yml. Superseded by the next complete release; see launch audit XR-LAUNCH-001.

stampTargets.comment: Installer-visible identity (what .msi/.dmg metadata shows). Added in launch-audit L-008 — previously unguarded.
Cargo package version; drifted to 0.2.0 before L-008 (Tauri reads conf version, but the shell's own crate identity must not lag).

claims.text: Runs locally with local models; no mandatory cloud control plane.
claims.evidence: src/providers/presets.ts — local runtimes (ollama, lmstudio, llamacpp, jan, localai, vllm) are first-class provider presets; src/config/config.ts localModels.

claims.text: Bring your own API key — provider credentials stay in your environment.
claims.evidence: src/config/config.ts provider apiKeyEnv resolution; secrets redacted by src/baseline/status.ts:redactValue.

claims.text: Per-task budget ceilings in USD and tokens, enforced during the agent loop.
claims.evidence: src/core/agent.ts budget enforcement; src/services/budget-service.ts; test/cost.test.ts.

claims.text: Hash-chained local audit log with a verification command.
claims.evidence: src/commands/audit.ts (verify); audit repo hash chain; test suite covers audit verification.

claims.text: 65 bundled skills.
claims.evidence: Directory count of skills/ at release commit — verified mechanically by scripts/claim-lint.ts (countSkills).

claims.text: Multiple model providers behind one interface; no vendor lock-in.
claims.evidence: src/providers/presets.ts and src/providers/registry.ts — provider-agnostic Provider interface.

claims.text: Plugin host and MCP client, available from CLI and interactive surfaces.
claims.evidence: src/plugins/manager.ts, src/mcp/manager.ts, src/services/agent-service.ts extraTools; test/phase0/surface-parity.test.ts.

claims.text: Written in TypeScript, running on Bun.
claims.evidence: package.json engines.bun; tsconfig.json; zero Rust sources in the repository.

claims.text: Tagged releases ship cosign keyless signatures over SHA256SUMS, a CycloneDX SBOM and SLSA3 provenance for every per-target artifact.
claims.evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml (gates → 5-target matrix → SHA256SUMS → cosign sign-blob → SLSA generator_generic_slsa3 with wired outputs.digests); docs/release/VERIFYING_RELEASES.md. Verifiable from the public Rekor log after the first tagged release ≥ 1.0.0.

claims.text: Every channel in channels.claimed serves the same canonical build of channels.publicVersion, with channel configs generated from one manifest; channels not yet live (Homebrew tap, WinGet review) are marked pending in the README install table.
claims.evidence: scripts/channel-manifest.ts (one generator) + packaging/ (generated, drift-gated by `bun run channel:check` in CI) + scripts/channel-live-check.ts (`bun run channel:live`: every claimed channel resolved against the live registry and the signed SHA256SUMS) run daily by .github/workflows/channel-live.yml + .github/workflows/channel-install.yml (real installs of the public version; .deb is dpkg-installed on every PR).

claims.text: XR Personal is free forever, with every local feature included and no account required.
claims.evidence: website/src/app/pricing/page.tsx; docs/business/BILLING.md §1; src/cloud/license.ts BUSINESS_FEATURES contains only hosted surfaces.

claims.text: XR Business is $15 per user per month, or $144 per user per year ($12 per month equivalent).
claims.evidence: website/src/lib/native.ts businessPricing; cloud/src/services/stripe.ts; docs/business/BILLING.md §2.

claims.text: A 30-day Business trial needs no card and covers up to 5 seats.
claims.evidence: cloud/src/routes/billing.ts trial config; cloud/src/env.ts TRIAL_DAYS/TRIAL_MAX_SEATS; docs/business/BILLING.md §3.

claims.text: Enterprise is quoted per contract and invoiced manually; there is no self-serve Enterprise checkout and no support SLA is offered.
claims.evidence: docs/business/BILLING.md §4 (NET 30 placeholder, contact sales only).

claims.text: SSO (OIDC and SAML 2.0) is available on the Business tier as an organization feature.
claims.evidence: cloud/src/services/sso.ts; cloud/src/routes/sso.routes.ts; docs/business/SSO.md; SAML SP metadata is generated from API_URL at /auth/sso/saml/{orgId}/metadata.

claims.text: Managed cloud models are an optional Business feature; BYOK remains free and direct-to-provider on every plan.
claims.evidence: cloud/src/services/metering.ts; cloud/src/routes/models.routes.ts; src/cloud/client.ts; docs/business/BILLING.md §5.

claims.text: A Business licence is a signed token verified offline against a key built into XR; no check-in is required and no remote kill switch exists.
claims.evidence: src/cloud/license.ts (node:crypto Ed25519, no network); test/cloud/license.test.ts asserts zero dial attempts.

claims.text: Cancelling leaves all local data intact; hosted team data stays exportable for 30 days and is then purged.
claims.evidence: cloud/src/services/subscriptions.ts cancellation path; website/src/app/legal/privacy/page.tsx; docs/business/BILLING.md §6.

claims.text: The website ships no third-party analytics, no advertising pixels and no tracking scripts.
claims.evidence: website has no analytics dependency (website/package.json); K is server logs only.

claims.text: XR contains no DRM, no obfuscation and no remote disable of local features.
claims.evidence: src/cloud/license.ts header comment; BUSINESS_FEATURES is the complete gate list and contains no local surface.

prohibitedClaims.reason: XR holds no SOC 2 audit. Type I is in progress and Type II is not attempted; neither may be written as though it were held. Article XIX forbids false certification claims.
XR holds no ISO 27001 certification.
XR has no HIPAA compliance program or BAA.
XR holds no PCI-DSS attestation.
XR holds no FedRAMP authorization.
The repository ships 65 skills. Use the mechanically-verified skills-count claim.
XR contains no Rust. It is TypeScript on Bun.
Fabricated GitHub star count.
Meaningless security superlative.
XR enforces in-process policy, not kernel isolation. Isolation is a later phase.
Absolute security claims are never evidenceable.
No SLA or dedicated support exists. XR is free, MIT-licensed and self-hosted; there is no commercial support organization.
No commercial SLA exists. Business OS modules are MIT-licensed extensions, not a paid tier.
XR contains no Rust (TypeScript on Bun). The website blog asserted this fabrication; removed by the Phase 10 claim audit.
Fabricated usage-scale claim. XR has no telemetry pipeline that could measure agent-run counts.
Fabricated feedback-scale claim; no mechanism exists to count developer feedback sessions.
XR is labeled public-beta in release.manifest.json. 'Generally available' is an unsupported release label (Article XXII.4).
Unsupported social-proof claim. No customer or regulated-industry adoption evidence exists.
No hosted VPC offering exists; XR is self-hosted by the deployer.
No commercial support organization exists.
The XR source remains MIT-licensed with no commercial source licence; the Business tier is a hosted service, not a licence for the software. Do not describe the software as commercially licensed.
Audit retention is configurable per event class (src/enterprise/audit/retention.ts), not a fixed hosted-tier feature.
XR is an application-layer AI agent runtime with in-process policy enforcement, not an operating system. OS-scale isolation is XR-OS roadmap work, not the runtime's identity (launch finding A-3).
XR ships a runtime kernel (DI container, lifecycle, stores) — not an OS kernel. Framing it as one is misleading (launch finding A-3).
Absolute security claims are never evidenceable. XR ships verifiable evidence — hash-chained audit (xr verify-log) and signed attack-screen reports (xr attacks) — not proofs of security.
Business OS is an optional, default-off, effect-verified extension over local-first records (extensions/business-os), not an operating system (launch finding A-3).
Personal is free forever and fully functional. It is never 'limited', never a trial, and no local feature is gated behind an upgrade. Article XXIX/XXX; Phase 30 §L.
Local features are free on every plan, signed in or not. Nothing may be described as requiring Business, subscription or an upgrade (Phase 30 §L: a constitutional bug, not a copywriting slip).
Nothing local requires an account, a sign-in, a subscription or a licence. XR works identically signed out.
No watermarks, no nags, no popups and no feature gates exist in any tier (Phase 30 §L).
XR has no telemetry pipeline and the website ships no third-party analytics in Phase 30. Server logs are the only telemetry and they are not person-linked.
